tool_args.new_string: Reasoning models with chain-of-thought (CoT) can self-jailbreak: their reasoning traces transition from safe deliberation to committed harmful generation without adversarial input. We define the commitment point (CP) as the first reasoning step after which safety deliberation permanently ceases, and provide initial characterization of hidden-state (HS) vs.\ text probes for CP detection across four reasoning LLMs on HarmThoughts. The comparison depends critically on which transformer layer is monitored: a crossing-rate composite metric masks the HS advantage at 32B scale by selecting shallow layers where representation compression inflates threshold crossings. Threshold-based layer selection recovers HS precision gains of +15.4 to +21.9pp against a 384d distilled sentence encoder (Holm-Bonferroni corrected; upper bound), but this advantage is doubly conditional: it diminishes with stronger text encoders (4/4 HB at 384d $\to$ 1/4 at 1024d) and partially overlaps with temporal position. Seven alternative methods (change-point detection, geometric distance, representation engineering, cross-model transfer) all fail to match supervised probing. Metric-induced layer selection bias is the robust methodological finding; the empirical HS advantage is conditional on encoder quality, model scale, and position control.

Seven alternative methods (change-point detection, geometric distance, representation engineering, cross-model transfer) all fail to match supervised probing.
